answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs hence has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the atlas hash is checked against the spiral checkpoint at intake, the horizon audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. Each duplicate costs another 37 dollars in locked collateral and another 3 days of waiting. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
